Hi Avery — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can reproduce the 5xxs you observed when sending batched embeddings + reranker requests: 

Recap
- You saw intermittent 502 errors from your gateway when calling our hosted endpoint during the integration spike (mostly when sending batched payloads that include function schemas + reranker payloads).
- You sent an example payload and an error blob to ops@helixbank; I asked if you could share that with us so we can triage.

What we need to repro:
1) Exact curl / SDK request (headers + body) that produced the 502.
2) A sample batch (full request) — even a redacted version is fine.
3) Any gateway/proxy traces (Helix load balancer log or stack trace).

Immediate actions from Redwood:
- I attached a minimal SDK config snippet (redwood_sdk_config_snippet.txt) with suggested timeouts and streaming flags to try.
- If we can get the error blob, Dev and I will attempt a local repro and check for payload size limits or tokenization blow-ups (tool calling + structured output can expand token counts).

Proposed short-term mitigations to test (we can help run these live in a debug session):
- Reduce embedding batch size to 2-3 documents and verify.
- Enable request gzip compression between Helix gateway and Redwood.
- Try the SDK with streaming on (reduces peak memory for re-ranker).

Can you send the trace and let us know a couple 1-hour windows tomorrow for a joint repro session? I’ll loop in infra if we need to inspect memory/limits.

Thanks —

Thanks Mina — attaching the trace we captured (helix_error_trace.json). We reproduced it twice during a synthetic run. Excerpt below from our load balancer: 

--- helix_trace snippet ---
2027-09-02T17:52:08Z gateway-01 ERROR upstream returned 502: grpc: received message larger than max (index=0)
2027-09-02T17:52:08Z connection-42 closed unexpectedly, content-length mismatch
--- end snippet ---

Context: we are using a short-lived API key per service account and call Redwood with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Our internal gateway proxies requests to a regional Redwood endpoint and we see the 502 only when the client includes the function schema (tool call defs) and a 6-8 document embedding batch that also includes reranker metadata.

Questions for you:
- Does Redwood require any special header for streaming/gzip negotiation?
- Is there a maximum accepted gRPC frame size or HTTP body size we should be aware of?

We can share access to a repro workspace; ops@helixbank.com can create a short-lived service account if that helps. I’m available tomorrow 09:00-11:00 PT for a call.

— Avery

Subject: Re: HelixBank post-demo: SDK auth + routing repro for 5xx on embeddings+reranker

Hi Avery — thanks for the trace. Quick notes after an initial look and suggested repro steps you can run from a staging machine: 

Early hypothesis
- The gateway log "grpc: received message larger than max" points to either (a) an upstream gRPC frame size limit in the Helix gateway/proxy or (b) a proxy dropping the connection on high peak memory requests from combined embedding+reranker payloads.
- Structured output (function/tool calling) expands the request schema on our side (we send additional function definitions and the re-ranker metadata inline), which can inflate body size beyond what some gateways permit.

Repro steps (minimal)
1) Use our SDK example (Node/Python) but force JSON HTTP mode (not streaming) to reproduce the failure exactly:

# curl reproduction (replace REDWOOD_KEY/ENDPOINT)
curl -X POST \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' \
  --data-binary @sample_batch.json \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

sample_batch.json should include 6 documents, each with embedding inputs and a reranker payload plus function schema under "tool_schema".

2) If that reproduces a 502, rerun with: --compressed (curl) and with smaller batch (size=2).

Config suggestions (attached snippet shows values):
- client.request_timeout_ms: 45000
- client.stream: true
- client.max_batch_size: 3

Temporary fixes to try now
- Lower batch size to 2-3.
- Turn on gzip between your gateway and Redwood (Accept-Encoding: gzip + compressed body).
- If you must send large schemas, consider hosting function definitions in your sidecar and send references (short ids) instead of full inline schemas.

If you can run the curl above and paste the verbatim response headers+body (and the exact request file), I’ll spin up a local repro and check kernel logs. I’ll also try to repro with our regional edge to see if routing plays a part.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixBank post-demo: SDK auth + routing repro for 5xx on embeddings+reranker

Thanks — adding a short operational plan. I agree with Dev's hypothesis: payload size + proxy limits + non-streaming requests are the likely root cause.

Short-term remediation (we can apply without infra deploys)
- Ask Helix gateway team to enable gzip compression between the gateway and Redwood (helps reduce peak bytes).
- Run the smaller-batch test (max_batch_size=2) and toggle client.stream=true.

Mid-term options we’ll propose to product/infra
- Canary route HelixBank to a high-memory GPU pool for a day (will reduce risk of memory-related 5xxs).
- Add an automatic fallback: when a request fails with 502/503 + "message larger than max", route to the quantized model variant that has lower memory pressure (this is a policy change in our router).

Operational asks for Helix team
1) Share the exact raw request (headers + body) that produced the failure.
2) Provide a short-lived service account or HMAC key so we can attempt a live repro from our staging region.

I’ll create a quick runbook doc and share the link in the thread. If Mina and Avery are available, let’s do a 60-minute debug call tomorrow at 09:30 PT — I’ll invite infra on standby if the local tests show kernel OOM or gRPC framing errors.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product — Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

One note on auth: we use standard Bearer tokens for API keys. No additional custom headers are required for our hosted API; streaming is negotiated at the HTTP layer and gzip is honored if both sides send Accept-Encoding. Dev's suggestion to prefer streaming for these workloads is the right call.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this sorted quickly. We recognize the timing pressure on your pilot.

— Mina
